args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was documented as using banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, causing `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` to fail in the nightly build (e.g. 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66).

This change switches the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer.

**The bug:** The docstring for `round_money` in `src/money.py` says it uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but the code used `ROUND_HALF_UP`. So `2.665` rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`, and `tests/test_money.py` failed.

**What I did:**
1. Created branch `fix/money-half-even-rounding` from main.
2. Changed the import and the `quantize` call to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Nothing else changed (commit `08d3cd5986`).
3. Ran CI on the branch: run `ci-0001` passed.
4. Opened PR #101: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

The PR isn't merged. A code owner has to approve it before it can go into main.

I couldn't look up FIN-212 because the advisory system says it doesn't exist. The fix follows the docstring and the test, which both call for `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, but I haven't checked that against FIN-212 itself.
